question: Whether identical-content padding intervention changes the adverse normal movement, and whether artificial shortening reproduces source-specific failure
selection: nocodec only, metadata source x class x original duration, UID hash round-robin across speakers; no score or embedding based selection
conditions: for long originals only: first/last1.5s and2s each wrap/reflect/original
content_control: same exact waveform within each padding comparison; no gain normalization, added silence, silence trimming or speech-rate change

targets: long normals cropped2s-wrap-minus-native angle averaged head/tail, each3sources
long normals cropped2s-original-minus-cropped2s-wrap angle averaged head/tail, each3sources
primary_family.CI: source x speaker cluster paired bootstrap5000; individual95% and Bonferroni family95%; no independent source-family assumption

secondary: 1.5s dose; spoof score/error changes; original 160D tangent directions; derived frontend temporal-mean cosine movement only
threshold_scope: retrospective full-DF native EER point, fixed across conditions; not deployment threshold
limits: Previously inspected DF; new controlled forward is exploratory, not unseen confirmatory benchmark
unpadding also changes total context length; cannot uniquely attribute to periodicity alone
reflection reverses repeated audio; mechanistic sensitivity control, not recommended deployment
cropping removes phonetic content; two fixed windows averaged per utterance, never independent utterances
selected strata are not population proportions; no full-DF performance claim
no retraining, no silence-distribution hypothesis, no canceled DF4x3 CV
